subject: Urgent: Riverbend Health private deployment QPS regression & error spike
messages:
From: Sam Becker <sam.becker@riverbendhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: private deployment throughput regression — Riverbend Health

Team —

We're seeing a sudden regression on our private deployment in us-west1: sustained QPS down ~60% over the last 20 minutes with a simultaneous jump in p95/p99 latency and a cluster of 502/504 decoder errors. This started right after we rolled a firewall update at ~08:50.

Impact: several critical user flows are timing out; automated ingestion backlog is growing. We're attaching a small log bundle and a pcap snippet.

What we need immediately:
- Confirmation this looks like a network/transport issue vs. model runtime.
- Any temporary mitigations (config change, routing) you can apply to restore baseline.
- ETA for an ops-led plan we can run together.

I've included Amal (CTO) on the thread since this is user-facing.

Attachments: riverbend_log_bundle_20261209.tar.gz, pcap_sample_routed_12.pcap

Sam Becker
Head of SRE, Riverbend Health
sam.becker@riverbendhealth.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Becker <sam.becker@riverbendhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: private deployment throughput regression — Riverbend Health

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. We're escalating now. Laura (engineering) and Marissa (CS) are looped in.

Immediate plan:
1) Laura to triage and propose a short mitigation we can run with you.
2) If necessary, we can route critical traffic to a hosted fallback for 30 minutes while we remediate (requires Amal signoff).
3) Quick sync at 09:30 PT to align on steps; I'll host a call and share bridge.

Please keep pcap and any config changes handy. We'll avoid any disruptive action on your side unless requested.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Becker <sam.becker@riverbendhealth.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: private deployment throughput regression — Riverbend Health

Sam / Karthik —

I've started digging into the log bundle. Initial signals point to frequent gRPC retransmits and decoder stalls localized to a subset of nodes (3/12). Two hypotheses so far: MTU/fragmentation introduced by the firewall change, or an implicit TCP path MTU blackhole causing pipelined requests to stall and trigger backend decoder timeouts. The pattern doesn't look like a model weight or tokenizer regression.

Immediate asks for you (to narrow):
- Sample request-id: the one around 08:56 with 502s (we saw an id in your logs but need the exact string).
- Node hostname or private IP for one affected node (we only have traces for node-07 right now).

Short mitigations we can try in the next 30–45 mins (low risk):
- Lower max_batch_tokens to 32 for affected pool (reduces per-request size).
- Enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 on affected hosts (if you can toggle kernel param).
- If you prefer, we can temporarily route ~10% of production QPS to Redwood hosted endpoints while we verify fix.

I'm attaching a draft runbook for a staged tcp_mtu probing change and a small heap/profile we pulled. If we confirm MTU issues, the patch above has historically recovered throughput quickly.

Attachments: runbook_tcp_mtu_patch.md

Laura Bennett
Senior Software Engineer, Performance
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Sam Becker <sam.becker@riverbendhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: amal.rai@riverbendhealth.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:34:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: private deployment throughput regression — Riverbend Health

Laura — thanks, that matches our timeline. We confirmed a firewall rule push at 08:47 that changed MSS clamping behavior on the peering devices. We can flip tcp_mtu_probing but will need Redwood to guide the exact command and the safe rollout window.

Request from our side: if temporary routing to hosted will work, can Redwood take ~15% traffic for 30–60 minutes to give us headroom while we apply kernel changes? Also, what's the cost and any SLA implications? Amal (CTO) is on standby to approve cross-network work.

I'll send sample request-id: req_20261209_085658 later this minute and upload a pcap to the drive link.

Sam

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Riverbend Health private deployment QPS regression & error spike

Team — ops note and proposed runbook:

1) Quick containment (10–15 mins):
   - Apply tcp_mtu_probing=1 on affected nodes (sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1). This forces active probing and recovers when path MTU changes.
   - Reduce max_batch_tokens from 128 -> 32 for the affected pool (config change, no restart).

2) Canary (30 mins):
   - Enable config on 20% of nodes and monitor p95/p99 and 5xx rate.
   - If green, roll to remaining nodes in 10-min waves.

3) Fallback option (requires Amal signoff):
   - Route up to 15% of production QPS to Redwood hosted endpoints for 30–60 minutes (we'll create a temporary route policy and warm a small pool).
   - Operations will capture a short-term invoice for hosted usage; Finance/CS can discuss credits post-incident.

Runbook (draft): runbook_tcp_mtu_patch.md
Jira: RW-5821

I'll stand by on the bridge and can run the commands with Riverbend's SRE if you give the go.

Jonas Weber
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amal Rai <amal.rai@riverbendhealth.com>, Sam Becker <sam.becker@riverbendhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Riverbend executive summary & ask — temporary routing and credit approval

Amal — quick summary and executive ask:

Summary: After your firewall change at ~08:47 we observed a path MTU-related regression that reduced QPS ~60% and increased p95/p99 latency with decoder 502s on a subset of nodes. Engineering (Laura) has identified tcp_mtu_probing as an effective low-risk mitigation. Ops (Jonas) has a staged runbook ready.

Executive asks:
- Approve temporary routing of up to 15% of production QPS to Redwood hosted endpoints for 30–60 minutes to ensure user-facing flows remain healthy while Riverbend applies kernel config changes. This avoids user impact but will result in incremental hosted usage.
- If you approve the route, we'll coordinate the cutover at ~11:15 PT and run the canary immediately.
- Post-incident: Redwood is prepared to discuss a one-time service credit for the overflow time.

Marissa will follow up on commercial details. We need a short approval from you (Amal) to proceed. If you'd like a 15-minute bridge now, we'll open one and include engineering and ops.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
